cf.title: Small gaps in IoWorkerMain() error handling

input.subject: [PATCH] Small gaps in IoWorkerMain() error handling

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the panel at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproduction path, the two fixes are local to IoWorkerMain(), and they add no user-visible surface. Confidence is low because only message #1 exists, nobody has replied, and the code was not read.

brief.title: Fix two error-handling gaps in I/O worker DEBUG4 logging
brief.problem: In IoWorkerMain(), an error raised while emitting the DEBUG4 "processing IO" message leaves error_errno at 0, which trips Assert(error_errno != 0) or gives a misleading "read only 0 of N bytes" error. A SIGINT handled during the same message makes the worker exit with a dequeued IO never completed, so waiting backends hang. Both cases need DEBUG4 logging from I/O workers.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 sets error_errno (ENOENT, as the reopen failure path already uses) before error_ioh. Patch 0002 moves the DEBUG4 message below HOLD_INTERRUPTS(), so errfinish() cannot process a die interrupt in that window. Both patches target back branches through 18.
author_claims: The author hit the assertion by injecting errors from an emit_log_hook, and says ordinary users probably do not hit it.
Without assertions, a read fails with a misleading "read only 0 of N bytes" error.
The DEBUG4 message is the only place that processes interrupts before HOLD_INTERRUPTS().
Moving the message is less invasive than failing owned IOs from an exit callback, which suits backpatching.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. Nobody has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review.
unclear: The author says ENOENT is a poor errno when the failure is unrelated to the file, and leaves the choice open.
The thread does not show a test or reproduction script beyond the hand-made log hook.
The patch does not say whether other code between dequeue and HOLD_INTERRUPTS() can raise errors or process interrupts.
The thread does not say whether the exit-callback alternative was tried or measured.
search_queries: aio IO never completed worker exit

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Both commit messages say "Backpatch-through: 18", so the change lands in a stable branch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Patch 0002 relies on no later code adding interrupt processing between dequeue and HOLD_INTERRUPTS() in method_worker.c.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Both patches reorder statements in the per-IO loop of IoWorkerMain(); the panel found no added cost.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can any code between the dequeue and HOLD_INTERRUPTS(), other than the DEBUG4 message, raise an error or process interrupts?
Which errno should the handler report when the failure is unrelated to the file, given that message #1 calls ENOENT a poor fit?
Should master get the exit callback that fails owned IOs, with the smaller reordering used only for the back branch?
Can an injection point or a test module reproduce both failures without a hand-made emit_log_hook?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the AIO worker method and the interrupt handling of auxiliary processes would have to own it. Nobody has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a change in a stable branch to the I/O worker error and interrupt path. A mistake there could cause wrong IO completion or hangs, and the reordering must keep holding as code is added later.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way. Message #1 leaves the errno choice and the exit-callback alternative open, which suggests the author expects to revise.

priority.reason: Both failures need DEBUG4 logging from I/O workers, so few installations can hit them, but one of them hangs backends. The two patches are under 2 KiB each, touch one file and add no user-visible surface.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that the DEBUG4 message is the only interrupt-processing point before HOLD_INTERRUPTS() is unverified. Whether setting error_errno earlier changes any other error path also could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: s/shm_mq_iovec/struct iovec/
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the shm_mq module's own shm_mq_iovec struct with the standard POSIX struct iovec. The motivation was to remove a duplicate definition now that struct iovec can be used everywhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas argued that the two structs belong to separate APIs and should stay separate. Reusing struct iovec could tie shm_mq to POSIX limits such as IOV_MAX, and it would stop shm_mq from adding its own fields later. The author accepted this and marked the entry returned with feedback.
matched_queries: aio IO never completed worker exit
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
They serve a similar purpose,
but they belong to completely separate APIs; I think "incidental
deduplication" is the right term for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Test for function error in logrep worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a TAP test to src/test/subscription/t/100_bugs.pl for a logical replication apply worker that hit a failed Assert in pg_proc.c when a function called from a subscriber trigger raised an error. The test runs an insert on the publisher and checks that the subscriber logs the expected error instead of crashing.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the case did not justify a permanent test. The crash came from a speculative Assert that had already been removed, and he saw no need for a test to stop it from coming back. He said that adding tests of this kind makes the suite slow enough that developers cannot run it easily. The author withdrew the entry after this reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we need a test
case to keep us from putting back the Assert.  That line of thinking
leads to test suites that run for fourteen hours and are near useless
because developers can't run them easily.

precedents_retrieved.title: Asynchronous and "direct" IO support for PostgreSQL
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), David Rowley (davidrowley), Thomas Munro (macdice)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Andres Freund proposed an asynchronous IO (AIO) subsystem for Postgres, with several backends (worker processes, io_uring, posix AIO, Windows) and helpers for streaming reads and writes. The same work adds optional direct IO, so data moves between storage and shared buffers without the kernel page cache.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry died of inactivity. The patch set stopped applying in January 2022 and no rebased version followed. In May 2022 Aleksander Alekseev asked for a rebase and said a set of 39 patches was too large to review, and that it should be split. Michael Paquier marked it Returned with feedback after five months without activity.
matched_queries: aio IO never completed worker exit
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't know what's the exact status here, but as there has been no
activity for the past five months, I have just marked the entry as RwF
for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restart pg_usleep when interrupted
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sleep function, later named pg_usleep_non_interruptible, that restarts nanosleep() with the remaining time when a signal interrupts it, and stops once the requested time has passed. Vacuum cost delay would use it so the parallel vacuum leader sleeps the full delay even when parallel workers send it frequent progress messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after the thread questioned whether the extra code was worth it. Nathan Bossart noted that interrupts rarely hit a vacuum delay point and that rate-limiting worker progress reports to 1 Hz would remove most of them, and the uninterruptible sleep would make vacuum slower to react to SIGTERM or cancel. CF #5118 would also change how pg_usleep() handles these interrupts, so the author left the question to that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Is it really that important to delay with that level of accuracy?

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't ignore recovery conflict interrupt on blocked writing
precedents_retrieved.summary: On a standby, a backend blocked writing results to a stuck or dead client ignores interrupts, so its buffer pin can block WAL replay until the TCP retransmission timeout, which can be about 15 minutes. The patch makes ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() handle recovery conflict interrupts during a blocked write and terminate the session, with a new Perl module for raw protocol tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch did not promote the ERROR to FATAL, so the session was not really terminated. He also showed that the backend often reaches ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() with interrupts held, for example while sending an error message, and then the conflict is never resolved. The author posted a reworked approach on 2025-01-21. No reply follows in the visible messages, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Unfortunately I suspect that this means any protection we'd get from this version of the patch is rather incomplete - if the recovery conflict is triggered while not blocked, we'll ERROR out and report the message with interrupts held.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve handling of OOM errors in libpq making process hangling for COPY and bind (take 2)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes libpq hangs on out-of-memory errors while it parses COPY start and ParameterDescription messages. The parser leaves pqParseInput3 on error and keeps the first error message, so PQgetResult and PQexecFinish return the failure and do not wait for server input that will not come.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas committed the ParameterDescription fix but did not commit the COPY part. He could not see why the PQexecFinish change was needed, and he found that if getCopyResult() fails with OOM, libpq stays in COPY_IN mode while PQexec() returns NULL, so the next PQexec() fails with "another command is already in progress". Michael Paquier later reported that Heikki could not convince himself the change was sane for the COPY protocol, and planned more testing with tools that use COPY through libpq.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, libpq is already in PGASYNC_COPY_IN mode, but PQexec() returned NULL because of the OOM, so the application doesn't know that it's in copy mode.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving the latch handling between logical replication launcher and worker processes.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a lost wakeup in the logical replication launcher, which uses one latch for worker attach, worker exit and subscription creation, so a new subscription's apply worker can wait up to 180 seconds to start. The author listed three options and posted v2 using a separate latch for worker attach and exit, protected by a lock and owned only around each wait.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not state a closing reason. Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to v2 because it calls OwnLatch and DisownLatch often and nests latch waits across concurrent wakeup sources, and he proposed a flag in shared memory that ApplyLauncherMain checks before WaitLatch. The author agreed and posted a new patch for that approach, and Heikki Linnakangas noted that his proposed interrupts patches would make the fix simple. The thread ends there without a review of the new patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Additionally, handling multiple concurrently operating trigger sources with nested latch waits seems bug-prone, which I’d prefer to avoid from both a readability and safety perspective.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pruning never visible changes
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Greg Stark, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets heap pruning remove a committed tuple version that no other transaction could ever see, such as a row inserted and then updated in the same transaction. It removes such a tuple only when xmin equals xmax and the tuple is at the root of the HOT chain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said a safe version must check that the originating transaction has no snapshots that can still see the older row version, and doubted it would fire often enough to be worth the cost. Greg Stark pointed to commit 44e4bbf75d, which removed the same xmin == xmax special case because VACUUM could remove TOAST tuples that MVCC-safe CLUSTER still needs. Alvaro Herrera asked whether the patch was safe given that TOAST problem, and Simon Riggs agreed to replace it with a test case and a comment explaining why such rows cannot be removed.
matched_queries: aio IO never completed worker exit
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But this begs the question: is the proposed change safe, given that
ancient consideration?  I don't think TOAST issues have been mentioned
in this thread so far, so I wonder if there is a test case that verifies
that this problem doesn't occur for some reason.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The one listed row [P5] shares only the topic of interrupt handling. It is about a standby backend blocked on a client write, and its recorded reason (interrupts held while sending an error message) does not apply to moving an I/O worker DEBUG4 message below HOLD_INTERRUPTS(). Message #1 does not point to any earlier discussion of this fix.

The patches change no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output, psql behaviour or client-visible contract. They only reorder an errno assignment and a DEBUG4 message inside the I/O worker loop. The one visible effect is the errno reported in a rare error path, ENOENT, which the reopen failure path already uses.

The patches change only control flow inside IoWorkerMain(): the order of an errno assignment and of HOLD_INTERRUPTS(). They add no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or exported API change, so backpatching to 18 has no ABI or pg_upgrade concern from this angle.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Both paths need DEBUG4 logging from I/O workers, a SIGINT to an auxiliary process, or an emit_log_hook, and an unprivileged user can arrange none of these. The patches add no new access, data exposure or default.

Two small, local bugfixes in one file. They add no GUC, API, catalog or hot-path cost, and the code only runs when I/O workers log at DEBUG4. The exit-callback alternative in message #1 would also protect future code added between dequeue and HOLD_INTERRUPTS(); a committer might want it in master only, but that does not argue against these back-branch fixes. [P5] concerns a different interrupt path and does not apply.

This is a bug fix in IoWorkerMain() error handling. No existing feature, option or extension covers it, and an extension cannot change how the I/O worker orders its error state and interrupt holding. The only other approach discussed is the author's own exit-callback alternative, which is a design choice inside core and falls outside this angle.

This is a bug fix for an assertion failure and a possible backend hang, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. The trigger is rare and needs DEBUG4 logging from I/O workers, but the fix is small, the cost falls on nobody, and committers do not usually ask for field reports before fixing a hang.
